title: Site pullback transports coefficient-compatible target families and their Hom comparisons
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and the finite rings $A_j=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^j$ for $j\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the ordinary module-sheaf derived categories on the small etale or pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Bounded constructibility means [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] on the etale site and [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] on the pro-etale site. A complex has Tor interval $[a,b]$ if its derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$; $D^b_{ctf}$ means bounded constructible with some finite Tor interval [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For $i\ge j\ge1$, write $S_{i,j}=-\otimes^L_{A_i}A_j$ for the quotient scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Write $F_j=\nu_X^*$ at coefficient $A_j$, for $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and $H_j^\tau(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_{A_j}(U,V)$ on the site $\tau=e,p$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}^\tau$. For $i\ge j\ge1$ let $\chi^{i,j}_T:F_jS^e_{i,j}T\xrightarrow{\sim}S^p_{i,j}F_iT$ be the canonical linear scalar/site comparison of [lem-coef-finite-hom-site-descent], let $\beta_j(U,V):F_jH^e_j(U,V)\to H^p_j(F_jU,F_jV)$ be the canonical evaluation-defined comparison of [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison], and let $v^{\tau,i,j}_{U,V}:S^\tau_{i,j}H^\tau_i(U,V)\to H^\tau_j(S^\tau_{i,j}U,S^\tau_{i,j}V)$ be the evaluation-defined quotient Hom comparison of [thm-coef-finite-hom] on the site $\tau$.

Fix $N\ge1$, objects $\Omega_j\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_j)$ for $1\le j\le N$, and isomorphisms $u_{i,j}:S^e_{i,j}\Omega_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_j$ for $N\ge i\ge j\ge1$ with $u_{i,i}=1$ and $u_{i,r}=u_{j,r}\circ S^e_{j,r}(u_{i,j})$, using the canonical scalar units and reassociations. Put $\Omega^p_j=F_j\Omega_j$ and
$$u^p_{i,j}=F_j(u_{i,j})\circ(\chi^{i,j}_{\Omega_i})^{-1}:S^p_{i,j}\Omega^p_i\longrightarrow\Omega^p_j.$$
Then the following hold.

(1) Each $\Omega^p_j$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_j)$ with the Tor interval of $\Omega_j$; each $u^p_{i,j}$ is an isomorphism; $u^p_{i,i}=1$ and $u^p_{i,r}=u^p_{j,r}\circ S^p_{j,r}(u^p_{i,j})$, using the canonical pro-etale scalar units and reassociations.

(2) For $\tau=e,p$, with $\Omega^e_j=\Omega_j$ and $u^e_{i,j}=u_{i,j}$, and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_\tau,A_i)$, put $h^{\tau,i,j}_K=H^\tau_j(S^\tau_{i,j}K,u^\tau_{i,j})\circ v^{\tau,i,j}_{K,\Omega^\tau_i}$. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_i)$ the following equality of morphisms $F_jS^e_{i,j}H^e_i(K,\Omega_i)\to H^p_j(F_jS^e_{i,j}K,\Omega^p_j)$ holds:
$$\beta_j(S^e_{i,j}K,\Omega_j)\circ F_j\bigl(h^{e,i,j}_K\bigr)=H^p_j\bigl(\chi^{i,j}_K,1\bigr)\circ h^{p,i,j}_{F_iK}\circ S^p_{i,j}\bigl(\beta_i(K,\Omega_i)\bigr)\circ\chi^{i,j}_{H^e_i(K,\Omega_i)}.$$

(3) Put $D^\tau_jT=H^\tau_j(T,\Omega^\tau_j)$ and let $\delta^\tau_T:T\to D^\tau_jD^\tau_jT$ be the transpose of $\operatorname{ev}^\tau_T\circ\sigma_{T,D^\tau_jT}$, where $\sigma$ is the signed tensor symmetry. For every $T\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_j)$, under the tensor comparison $F_j(U\otimes^L_{A_j}V)\cong F_jU\otimes^L_{A_j}F_jV$ one has $\operatorname{ev}^p_{F_jT}\circ(\beta_j(T,\Omega_j)\otimes1)=F_j(\operatorname{ev}^e_T)$, and
$$\beta_j(D^e_jT,\Omega_j)\circ F_j(\delta^e_T)=H^p_j\bigl(\beta_j(T,\Omega_j),1\bigr)\circ\delta^p_{F_jT}.$$
These assertions refer to transported targets and do not posit an ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint.

proof.text: Specialize the current [lem-coef-finite-hom-site-descent] to $n=m=j$, so $A=B=R=A_j$, for each $\Omega_j$. Its hypotheses hold: $X$ is separated finite type over the fixed field, $\ell\ne p$, and $\Omega_j$ is bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude on the etale site. Its preservation clause gives $F_j\Omega_j\in D^b_{ctf}$ with every Tor interval possessed by $\Omega_j$. For $n=i$, $m=j$ the same lemma makes each $\chi^{i,j}$ a natural linear isomorphism; functoriality preserves the given isomorphism $u_{i,j}$. Hence $u^p_{i,j}=F_j(u_{i,j})(\chi^{i,j}_{\Omega_i})^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. This proves the object and invertibility assertions in (1).

source.place: Finite pro-etale realization: transport of the target objects and quotient maps

proof.text:
For $i\ge j\ge r\ge1$, specialize the descent lemma to $A=A_i$, $B=A_j$, $C=A_r$. For the cocycle suppress scalar reassociators and write $\chi^{i,r}_T=S^p_{j,r}(\chi^{i,j}_T)\circ\chi^{j,r}_{S^e_{i,j}T}$, the successive-quotient coherence of [lem-coef-finite-hom-site-descent]. Naturality at $u_{i,j}$ gives
$$ (\chi^{j,r}_{\Omega_j})^{-1}\circ S^p_{j,r}F_j(u_{i,j})=F_rS^e_{j,r}(u_{i,j})\circ(\chi^{j,r}_{S^e_{i,j}\Omega_i})^{-1}. $$
Substituting this in the definitions yields
$$u^p_{j,r}\circ S^p_{j,r}(u^p_{i,j})=F_r\bigl(u_{j,r}\circ S^e_{j,r}(u_{i,j})\bigr)\circ(\chi^{i,r}_{\Omega_i})^{-1}=u^p_{i,r}.$$
For $u^p_{i,i}=1$ take $i=j=r$ in that coherence: identifying $S_{i,i}$ with the identity by the scalar units (naturality of $\chi^{i,i}$ at these units), it reads $\chi^{i,i}_T=\chi^{i,i}_T\circ\chi^{i,i}_T$, so the isomorphism $\chi^{i,i}$ is the unit identification; with $u_{i,i}=1$ this gives $u^p_{i,i}=1$.

source.place: 'The cocycle is their quotient cocycle': explicit transport of the target cocycle

proof.text:
Use the evaluation-defined $\beta$ of [def-sf-evaluation-hom-site-comparison] and the natural tensor-Hom bijection of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. For $L=S^e_{i,j}K$ and $u=u_{i,j}$, naturality in the second Hom variable reads
$$\beta_j(L,\Omega_j)\circ F_jH^e_j(L,u)=H^p_j(F_jL,F_ju)\circ\beta_j(L,S^e_{i,j}\Omega_i).$$
Indeed, untransposing either side gives $F_j(u)$ composed with pulled-back evaluation at $(L,S^e_{i,j}\Omega_i)$, using naturality of the tensor comparison. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the equation. This uses the comparison's definition, without requiring its invertibility.

source.place: 'the two comparisons already proved': naturality for changing the transported target

proof.text:
Apply the square in the current [lem-coef-finite-hom-site-descent] with $n=i$, $m=j$, $(K,M)=(K,\Omega_i)$. Both inputs satisfy its etale $D^b_{ctf}$ hypothesis. The square is an equality of canonical evaluation-defined maps and requires no invertibility of either $v$; its $h$ is our $\chi^{i,j}$. Abbreviate $\chi_K=\chi^{i,j}_K$ and $\chi_\Omega=\chi^{i,j}_{\Omega_i}$. It says
$$v^p\circ S^p_{i,j}(\beta_i)\circ\chi^{i,j}_{H^e_i(K,\Omega_i)}=H^p_j(\chi_K^{-1},\chi_\Omega)\circ\beta_j(S^e_{i,j}K,S^e_{i,j}\Omega_i)\circ F_j(v^e).$$
Postcompose with $H^p_j(\chi_K,u^p_{i,j})$. Bifunctoriality cancels $\chi_K^{-1}\chi_K$ in the first variable and replaces $u^p_{i,j}\chi_\Omega$ by $F_j(u_{i,j})$ in the second. The right side is therefore $H^p_j(F_jS^e_{i,j}K,F_j u_{i,j})\beta_j(S^e_{i,j}K,S^e_{i,j}\Omega_i)F_j(v^e)$, which step 3 identifies with $\beta_j(S^e_{i,j}K,\Omega_j)F_j(h^{e,i,j}_K)$. The left side becomes exactly the right side of (2), since $H^p_j(\chi_K,u^p)=H^p_j(\chi_K,1)H^p_j(S^p_{i,j}F_iK,u^p)$. All objects are on the required sites: step 1 gives $F_iK,\Omega^p_i\in D^b_{ctf}$, so both instances of $v$ in [thm-coef-finite-hom] apply.

source.place: Finite pro-etale realization of the coefficient-Hom map with its transported target

proof.text:
For the remaining clause fix $j$, write $F=F_j$, $W=\Omega_j$, $Q=H^e_j(T,W)$ and $c=\beta_j(T,W)$. The evaluation identity
$$\operatorname{ev}^p_{FT}\circ(c\otimes1)=F(\operatorname{ev}^e_T)$$
is the defining untranspose in [def-sf-evaluation-hom-site-comparison], using the closed adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. It is valid for every first argument, in particular for $Q$. For the finite-Tor comparison clauses one can also check its domain: [thm-coef-finite-hom] with $A=B=A_j$ says $Q\otimes^L_{A_j}A_j$ is in $D^b_{ctf}$, hence $Q$ is in $D^b_{ctf}$ under the scalar unit. Thus both pairs $(T,W)$ and $(Q,W)$ have first argument in $D^b_{ctf}$ and second in $D^b_c$, the range where the statement names $\beta_j$, and there $\beta_j$ is this evaluation transpose; its invertibility is not used.

source.place: 'Evaluation compatibility follows from the two comparisons already proved': evaluation for the object and its first dual

proof.text:
Put $d=\beta_j(Q,W)$ and compare $d\circ F(\delta^e_T)$ with $H^p_j(c,1)\circ\delta^p_{FT}$ by untransposing into the common target $H^p_j(FQ,FW)$. The natural adjunction and symmetry are [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], $\nu_X$ is a morphism of ringed sites for the constant rings $A_j$ with module pullback $F$, so by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] its canonical tensor comparison $\mu$ is natural and symmetric: $\mu\circ F(\sigma_{U,V})=\sigma_{FU,FV}\circ\mu$, with the signed symmetry on both sites. For the first morphism its untranspose is
$$F(\operatorname{ev}^e_Q)\circ(F\delta^e_T\otimes1)=F(\operatorname{ev}^e_Q\circ(\delta^e_T\otimes1))=F(\operatorname{ev}^e_T)\circ\sigma_{FT,FQ}.$$
Here naturality of $\mu$ moves $F\delta^e_T\otimes1$ inside $F$, and the definition of $\delta^e_T$ together with $\mu\circ F(\sigma_{T,Q})=\sigma_{FT,FQ}\circ\mu$ gives the last equality. For the second morphism, naturality of evaluation in its first variable and the definition of $\delta^p_{FT}$ give
$$\operatorname{ev}^p_{FT}\circ\sigma_{FT,D^p_jFT}\circ(1\otimes c)=\operatorname{ev}^p_{FT}\circ(c\otimes1)\circ\sigma_{FT,FQ}=F(\operatorname{ev}^e_T)\circ\sigma_{FT,FQ}.$$
The last equality is step 5. Both use the same signed symmetry $\sigma_{FT,FQ}$, so the untransposes agree. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves (3). No step asserts that $\delta_T$ is invertible or constructs an exceptional adjoint.

lean.statement: theorem coefFiniteSiteHomTransport (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ D.p) (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] (N : ℕ) (Ω : ∀ i : Fin (N + 1), finiteHomEtale l E X i.val) (uΩ : ∀ (i j : Fin (N + 1)) (h : j.val ≤ i.val), (finiteHomEtaleReduction l E X h).obj (Ω i) ≅ Ω j) (_hΩ : ∀ i : Fin (N + 1), finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (i.val + 1) (Nat.succ_pos i.val) X (Ω i)) (_hunit : ∀ i : Fin (N + 1), (uΩ i i (Nat.le_refl i.val)).hom = (coefFiniteSiteEtaleUnit l E X i.val).hom.app (Ω i)) (_hcocycle : ∀ (i j r : Fin (N + 1)) (h : j.val ≤ i.val) (k : r.val ≤ j.val), (finiteHomEtaleAssoc l E X h k).hom.app (Ω i) ≫ (uΩ i r (k.trans h)).hom = (finiteHomEtaleReduction l E X k).map (uΩ i j h).hom ≫ (uΩ j r k).hom) : CoefFiniteSiteTargetTransport l E X N Ω uΩ
lean.note: Positive exponents are indexed by n+1; Fin (N+1) covers every nonempty finite range. Helpers only name the specified target transitions, Hom composites and three conclusion formulas. Identity and cocycle equations use the published scalar units and reassociators. The signed symmetry witnesses are normalized on the existing total-tensor models, not input hypotheses. Small pro-etale object/morphism universes remain distinct; no exceptional adjoint is introduced.
